drhp.business: Park Medi World operates a network of 14 NABH-accredited multi-super-specialty hospitals across Haryana, New Delhi, Punjab and Rajasthan under the 'Park' brand, offering over 30 super-specialty and specialty services. It serves largely lower-middle and middle-class patients, with revenue heavily weighted to government schemes/PSUs, and has grown through a cluster-based mix of organic build-out and hospital acquisitions.
drhp.end_markets: Government schemes and PSUs (88.46% of revenue FY25)|Self-pay / individual patients (6.40% FY25)|Insurance (5.01% FY25)
drhp.expansion: Bed capacity grew from 2,550 (Mar 2023) to 3,250 (Sep 2025); pipeline in Ambala, Panchkula, Rohtak, New Delhi, Gorakhpur and Kanpur. Ambala expanding from 250 to 450 beds plus onco-radiation (operational by Oct 2027); Panchkula 300-bed hospital (by Apr 2026); Rohtak 250-bed hospital (by Dec 2026); Gorakhpur 400-bed O&M hospital (by Apr 2026); Kanpur 300-bed hospital under renovation (by Apr 2026). Company expects total bed capacity to rise to 4,900 beds by March 31, 2028.

strengths_observed: Second largest private hospital chain in North India and largest in Haryana by bed capacity (3,250 beds as of Sep 2025 across 14 NABH-accredited hospitals)
Demonstrated track record of acquiring and integrating hospitals (8 acquisitions, 1,650 beds added); acquired hospitals contributed 55.12% of revenue and 61.90% of PAT in H1 FY26

Predominantly owns hospital assets; lowest gross block per bed among listed peers (Rs 3.44 million vs peer average Rs 10.64 million) and reportedly second-highest EBITDA margin among peers in FY2025 per CRISIL
Operates in a structurally under-served, fast-growing North India healthcare delivery market (region projected 12-14% CAGR to FY2029)
Diversified specialty mix (30+ services) and improving ARPOB (Rs 24,575 FY23 to Rs 27,105 H1 FY26)
Doctor-led promoter/management team; deleveraging intent with Rs 3,800 million of Net Proceeds earmarked for debt repayment

sk.overview: The dialysis services market provides life-sustaining renal replacement therapy (primarily in-clinic haemodialysis) for patients with chronic kidney disease and End Stage Renal Disorder. Demand is driven by the rising global burden of diabetes, hypertension and CKD, an ageing population and improved diagnosis. In India the market is largely underpenetrated (only ~1 in 15 ESRD patients access dialysis) and dominated (~80%) by standalone private and government clinics, with organized chains accounting for ~20%.
